hpi_details: Presents via emergency ambulance in severe acute respiratory distress, sitting upright leaning forward, unable to speak in full sentences. medications: ramipril 10mg OD, bisoprolol 5mg OD, furosemide 40mg OD

clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Cardiogenic Pulmonary Oedema evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Cardiogenic Pulmonary Oedema is essential for appropriate diagnostic workup and treatment.
Clinical history, severity assessment, and targeted testing must be interpreted together rather than relying on one symptom alone.
Provide immediate upright positioning, oxygen only when hypoxaemic, and ventilatory support when needed.
Management should follow local pathways and account for patient-specific comorbidity and clinical severity.

common_misconceptions: Assuming a mild or atypical presentation rules out Acute Cardiogenic Pulmonary Oedema.
Relying on a single normal test result to prematurely exclude serious pathology.
Equating transient symptom improvement with resolution of the underlying condition.
Failing to consider clinically important alternative diagnoses.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before appropriate assessment.
Starting treatment without considering contraindications, interactions, or organ function.
Ignoring critical warning signs: Severe respiratory distress or hypoxaemia.
management_principles: Provide immediate upright positioning, oxygen only when hypoxaemic, and ventilatory support when needed.
Treat congestion and the precipitant with urgent senior assessment, diuretics, and vasodilators when clinically appropriate.
Evaluate for acute coronary syndrome, arrhythmia, hypertensive emergency, and renal dysfunction.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 67M with prior MI and HTN presents with acute-onset severe nocturnal dyspnoea, pink frothy expectoration, orthopnoea, and acute respiratory distress.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: severe tachypnoea RR 34, tachycardia HR 122, severe hypoxaemia O2 sat 81% on room air, severe acute hypertension BP 195/110 mmHg (sympathetic surge). Physical exam: patient sitting bolt upright, cold clammy diaphoretic skin, marked peripheral cyanosis. Cardiovascular exam: JVP markedly elevated (+6 cm H2O), loud S3 gallop rhythm heard at apex. Respiratory auscultation: loud, coarse, bubbling inspiratory and expiratory crackles heard throughout all lung fields ('wet lungs' from apex to base), plus cardiac wheeze ('cardiac asthma'). Erect Chest X-ray (or portable): demonstrates classical Acute Pulmonary Oedema / Congestive Heart Failure signs ('ABCDE' -> Alveolar bat-wing/butterfly perihilar shadowing, Kerley B lines in costophrenic angles, Cardiomegaly, Dilated upper lobe pulmonary vessels / upper lobe diversion, and pleural Effusions). 12-lead ECG: sinus tachycardia, broad Q waves anteriorly, and acute ST-segment depressions in lateral leads (subendocardial ischemia). Bloods: NT-proBNP markedly elevated (>5000 pg/mL confirming acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema), urgent troponin, U&Es, ABG (severe hypoxaemia with metabolic lactic acidosis).
reference_soap.assessment: Acute Cardiogenic Pulmonary Oedema (Acute Decompensated Heart Failure triggered by hypertensive emergency / acute ischemia). DDx: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS -> non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema with normal PCWP and absent S3/JVP), severe COPD/asthma exacerbation (ruled out by pink frothy sputum and bat-wing CXR), acute bilateral pneumonia.
reference_soap.plan: This is a medical emergency requiring immediate senior/emergency-team management. Keep the patient upright, continuously monitor oxygenation, ventilation, ECG, blood pressure, and renal function, and evaluate urgently for acute coronary syndrome, arrhythmia, hypertensive emergency, and other precipitants. Clinicians may provide oxygen for hypoxaemia and select non-invasive ventilation, diuretics, or vasodilators only after assessment of oxygenation, blood pressure, contraindications, renal function, and response. Escalate to critical care if respiratory failure, altered consciousness, shock, or failure of initial support develops.

learning_objectives: Identify classical physical and radiographic signs of acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema: pink frothy sputum, S3 gallop, and bat-wing CXR
Recognize the need for immediate clinician-led ventilatory and circulatory support in severe pulmonary oedema
Explain why diuretics and vasodilators require haemodynamic, renal, and contraindication assessment
Differentiate cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (high NT-proBNP, elevated JVP) from non-cardiogenic ARDS

teaching.one_liner: Acute left-sided heart failure causing pulmonary fluid accumulation, severe dyspnoea, and pink frothy sputum.
red_flags: Hypotension, altered consciousness, or ongoing chest pain

must_ask.objective: Sudden onset of dyspnea and pink frothy sputum
must_ask.say: You said this started very suddenly two hours ago - can you describe what came up when you coughed?
Do you need to sit up or use extra pillows to breathe comfortably at night?

must_ask.objective: Cardiac history and prior myocardial infarction
must_ask.say: You've had a heart attack before - have you had any chest pain or pressure with this episode?
Have you been taking your heart and blood pressure medicines, and eating a lot of salty food lately?

must_ask.objective: Renal function and fluid overload signs
must_ask.say: Have your legs been swelling up, or has your urine output changed recently?
